research_program: Christopher Daniel Pang, PAL. Derivations with Hearthline.

upstream_argument.description: Levent Alpöge and Claude, 20 November 2026 release

reading_editions.result: The Bernoulli-unit implication for arbitrary odd conductor holds at half the released sufficient dyadic conductor. Two signed Fourier rows differ by twice a unit. The next full halving fails at 17.
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Christopher Daniel Pang asked for the smallest observation that earns a claim and an independent test on the same arithmetic objects. The signed-sum calculation at 17 led Hearthline to two representatives on opposite sides of the midpoint.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: Alpöge and Claude provide the original general Bernoulli test and the endpoint-shift proof for their range. Hearthline reconstructed that argument, derived the two-row identity and stronger range, carried the pure boundary separately, and checked the coefficient identity symbolically. No literature priority claim is made.
